interface.signature: def createTree(parent: List[int], N: int) -> TreeNode:

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) for x in parent) and len(parent) == N
preconditions.description: The input `parent` is a list of integers of length exactly `N`.

preconditions.expression: all(-1 <= x < N for x in parent)
preconditions.description: Each element in `parent` is either -1 (root) or a valid node index in the range [0, N-1].
There is exactly one root node (value -1) in `parent`.
The size `N` of the tree is at least 1.

postconditions.expression: return_value is None or isinstance(return_value, TreeNode)
postconditions.description: The function returns either `None` or a `TreeNode` object representing the root of the constructed binary tree.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(node, TreeNode) for node in [return_value] + [node.left for node in _traverse(return_value)] + [node.right for node in _traverse(return_value)])
postconditions.description: Every node in the tree (including root, left children, and right children) is a valid `TreeNode` object, where `_traverse(root)` is a helper that returns all nodes in the tree (including `None` for missing children).

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= node.val < N for node in _traverse(return_value) if node is not None)
postconditions.description: Every node's `val` is a valid index in the range [0, N-1].

postconditions.expression: all((node.left is None or node.left.val == parent[node.val][0]) and (node.right is None or node.right.val == parent[node.val][1]) for node in _traverse(return_value) if node is not None)
postconditions.description: For every node, its left child (if exists) is the first child in `parent` with the node's index as parent, and its right child (if exists) is the second child in `parent` with the node's index as parent. Here, `parent[node.val]` is a list of children indices for `node.val` (left first, then right).

postconditions.expression: return_value is None or return_value.val == parent.index(-1)
postconditions.description: The root node's `val` is the index of the -1 in `parent` (i.e., the root's index).
